sentences.text: These two appeals are preferred by accused No.3 in Crime No.241/2016 and 258/2015 registered at Mandya West Police Station for the offence punishable under Section 420,406,409 of IPC r/w Section 9 of Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004 (Hereinafter referred to as KPIDFE Act, 2004.

entities.text: Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The appellants have preferred the Criminal Misc.No.559/2024 and Criminal Misc.No.560/2024 in crime No.258/2015 and 241/2016 respectively, of Mandya West Police Station under Section 438 of Cr.P.C to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.
3. The learned Sessions Judge vide order dated 17.09.2024, dismissed both the petitions.

The observation made by the learned judge at Para 4,5 reads as under:-
4.

"Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner, and the learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent (State).
5.

In view of the materials placed before me, the points that arise for my consideration are as follows:-
NC: 2024:KHC:41261 1) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the discretionary relief of anticipatory bail as prayed for?
2) what order?"
4.

The learned counsel for the petitioners in both cases would submit that the co-ordinate Bench of this Court has already allowed the appeals filed by the appellants in Criminal Appeal No.292/2024 connected with Criminal Appeal No.190/2024 vide order dated 13.03.2024.
Hence, on the ground of principle of parity, he sought for allowing these appeals also.
5. The learned HCGP has not disputed the order passed by the Co-ordinate bench of this Court in Criminal Appeal No.292/2024 connected with Criminal Appeal No.190/2024.
The co-ordinate Bench of this Court has already assigned reasons for allowing the appeal filed by the co-accused pertaining to the same crime number.
6. Considering the facts and circumstances of these case and also keeping in mind the principle of parity, it is just and proper to allow these appeals.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:-
NC: 2024:KHC:41261 ORDER Criminal Appeal No. 1758/2024 and Criminal Appeal No.1759/2024 are allowed.

The order dated 17.09.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. No.560/2024 and Criminal Misc.No.559/2024 by the Court of Principal District and Sessions Judge, Mandya are set aside subject to following conditions:
